title: Serve raw APK downloads with Android's package MIME type
problem: Nora's raw registry classifies .apk paths as application/octet-stream, so Android browsers cannot hand downloads directly to the package installer.
reproduce: Apply the unchanged source-contract test to the pinned baseline; the APK assertion fails because guess_content_type has no apk match arm.
acceptance: The baseline fails with APK_MIME_MISSING; the candidate maps .apk paths to application/vnd.android.package-archive while .aab and unknown extensions retain the octet-stream fallback.
repair: Add the registered Android package MIME type to the raw registry extension map, cover APK and AAB behavior in the production Rust unit test, and add the required changelog fragment.

verification.limitations: BCL proves the exact production source mapping with an immutable red/green test. The candidate's real Rust test, clippy and all 1,885 non-ignored project tests were also run locally; two permission tests require a non-root runner and passed separately there. One upstream GPG integration test remains ignored because gpg and gpgv are unavailable. Upstream CI remains the authoritative cross-platform build.
verification.ownerCheck: Upload an APK to the raw registry, download it from an Android browser, confirm the response Content-Type is application/vnd.android.package-archive and that Android offers the package installer.

publish.commitMessage: fix(raw): serve APK files with Android MIME type
